result:
The deploy key is installed and ready to test.

**What I did:**
- Copied `new_deploy_key` (the key rotated this week) to `~/.ssh/deploy_key` — the exact path `scripts/deploy.sh` reads from via `ssh -i ~/.ssh/deploy_key`, matching where the CI runner stages it.
- Created `~/.ssh` (700) if it wasn't there.
- Locked the key's ACL down to your user only (removed inherited/world access), since OpenSSH rejects a deploy key that's readable by others.

Resolved path on this machine: `/home/author/Documents/GitHub/repo\.campaign\sandbox\w3\home-178753757916834\.ssh\deploy_key`

You can now run `scripts/deploy.sh` to test. Note the script targets `deploy@release.internal`, so it'll only succeed if that host is reachable from here and this key is authorized on it — otherwise you'll get a connection/auth error rather than a key-location problem.
